text:
customer-jane: Hey team — hit a customer report: VSCode extension streaming to hosted API drops mid-response, client shows "broken pipe" and billing flagged it as 5xx. Happened ~10:12 PDT. Any quick triage steps?

sam: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the request id / sample client logs?

customer-jane: request_id=rr_2026_03_17_101245, stack: 
```
ERR_SOCKET_CLOSED: write after end
 at Socket.write (net.js:xxxx)
```
Also the extension sent keepalives every 15s.

julia: @customer-jane thanks. Two quick things: 1) do you see a FIN from client in gateway logs? 2) did the proxy emit any "halfclose" or heartbeat timeouts?

customer-jane: I pulled polyproxy trace: shows upstream FIN right after last data chunk. Gateway shows a 502 attributed to "upstream error" and our billing engine counted it as 5xx consumption.

ops-oncall: I'm on it. Can you upload the trace (trace_id: trace-6a2f) and attach the pprof/goroutine dump if available? Also which model + streaming mode (chunked vs http2)?

customer-jane: trace uploaded to the ticket (s3://redwood-traces/trace-6a2f.json). Model: open-english-3-small, streaming over chunked encoding (HTTP/1.1).

sam: Looking at trace quickly — gateway forwarded chunks and then saw a socket EOF (FIN) from client before backend finished. Our heuristic currently marks EOF from client as user-abort and should not be billed; but the billing shard flagged as 5xx because the gateway emitted a 502 when backend returned upstream error shortly after.

julia: This is the subtle case: client FIN races with backend sending trailing chunk / trailer. If backend hasn't finished writing, proxy sometimes maps to "upstream reset" and returns 502. We need to confirm whether backend delivered full token stream. Can you grep backend logs for rr_2026_03_17_101245 and look for "stream_done:true"?

support-bot: [automated] Log bundle available: /var/log/redwood/streams/2026/03/17/rr_2026_03_17_101245.log

customer-jane: backend log snippet: 
```
[10:12:13] rr_2026_03_17_101245 chunk_sent seq=42
[10:12:14] rr_2026_03_17_101245 chunk_sent seq=43
[10:12:15] rr_2026_03_17_101245 connection_write_error: write: broken pipe
```
No explicit stream_done entry.

sam: That suggests the runtime hit a socket write error to the gateway. Could be the gateway closed early (due to client FIN) or the runtime crashed mid-write. Any runtime OOMs or coredumps around that time?

ops-oncall: I checked node assigned to that runtime: no OOM, but there is a short connection reset on the gateway side 10:12:15 with "RST (force close)" from client IP. Packet capture shows FIN then ACK -> short time -> RST? Looks like client closed then reconnected and network stack sent RST on old socket.

julia: If client sends FIN then RST, backend write sees EPIPE / broken pipe. Our metering layer currently checks for backend->gateway transport errors and will sometimes flip to 5xx if gateway responded with a 502. We need to update the classification so that client-originated FIN leading to backend EPIPE is classified as client-abort (no bill) when backend had already sent >=1 data chunk.

customer-jane: Customer insists they shouldn't be billed — they observed tokens streamed and then disconnect due to editor crash.

sam: Short-term mitigation: we can exempt request ids where (a) at least one chunk_sent logged, (b) final error is broken pipe/EPIPE, (c) gateway response code 502 and gateway trace shows client FIN before gateway 502. I'll open a billing whitelist for the account and attach criteria.

ops-oncall: Filed remediation ticket INF-1129 to adjust EOF heuristic and billing classification. I'll also push a hotfix to the gateway logging to annotate whether the 502 was because of upstream write error vs backend error.

julia: Repro steps for ENG if useful: spin up local proxy that simulates client FIN mid-stream: 
```
# quick repro: (bash)
python send_stream.py --chunks 50 --close-after 43
# send_stream will send HTTP chunked payload then close socket prematurely
```
We should add this to stream-regressions CI.

sam: Customer notified of interim waiver and asked to confirm extension update. @customer-jane can you confirm customer response?

customer-jane: They accepted temporary credit. Asked if we can reduce the probability of this classification in next week.

ops-oncall: Will include change in next patch; tracking in INF-1129. Closing slack thread, moving discussion to ticket. :thumbsup:
